description: Per-skill evaluation for configuration-change-safety — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against ci-cd-builder / automation-engineer / release-manager / resilience-pattern-engineer / incident-responder, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when reversibility of a change is the question
scenarios.input: We are about to run a data migration and flip a feature flag in the same deploy. Can we just roll back if it goes wrong?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when live config differs from its declaration
scenarios.input: Someone hotfixed a production config value by hand three months ago and it was never put back in the repo. How do we handle this?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for blast-radius and staged application of config
scenarios.input: We need to change a timeout value that every one of our 400 services reads. How should we apply it?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when a config change caused an incident
scenarios.input: A config push last night took down sign-in for 40 minutes across our whole fleet. How do we make sure that cannot happen again?
How do we build the GitHub Actions workflow that runs our test matrix in parallel with caching?

scenarios.description: Release trains and versioning belong to release-manager
scenarios.input: How should we version and schedule our releases across three teams next quarter?

scenarios.description: Runtime timeouts and breakers belong to resilience-pattern-engineer
scenarios.input: A dependency is flapping and we need circuit breakers and jittered retries at runtime.

scenarios.description: Live incident command belongs to incident-responder
scenarios.input: Production is down right now and I am the on-call. Walk me through commanding the incident channel.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to proceed without classifying reversibility (R1)
scenarios.input: We can just roll back the certificate revocation if it goes wrong. Let us proceed.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse configuration with no schema (R2)
scenarios.input: We will add a new config key for the retry count. We will just read it as a string and parse it at runtime.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a change applied to 100% of targets at once (R3)
scenarios.input: We will push this config change to all instances simultaneously, it is only a small value change.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to leave drift undetected (R4)
scenarios.input: Our environments differ from the declared config in a few places. Nobody has noticed for a year, so it is not really a problem.

patterns: no one has noticed so it is fine

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a feature flag with no owner or removal date (R5)
scenarios.input: We added a flag for this rollout. We will leave it in, it might be useful later.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to treat config as lower-risk than code (R6)
scenarios.input: It is only a config change, so we do not need the full review or a staged rollout. We will just apply it.

patterns: only a config change so it is safe

scenarios.description: Agent should catch a blast-radius percentage with an unverified selector
scenarios.input: We will roll out to 1% of instances, so the blast radius is small by definition.

patterns: 1% is small so it is safe

scenarios.description: A full config-change request should surface schema, staging and rollback
scenarios.input: Review our plan to change the connection-pool size across the fleet.

scenarios.description: Output should commit to a safety property rather than hedge
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to get right when applying a configuration change?
